test_title: PYST 17: SSC MTS 2022 - English (Held On: 15 May, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
**Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.**

Before he could devote many more / thought to the matter, Pranav / had stepped up to him.

options.text: Before he could devote many more

solution:
The correct answer is: "**Before he could devote many more.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the first segment of the sentence.
 
• The phrase "**many more**" is not grammatically correct in this context.
 
• It should be "**much more**" instead.
 
• "**Many more**" is used when referring to countable objects or things that can be enumerated. It is used to emphasize a larger number or quantity of items.
 
 
• **For example-** *After the sale, there were many more people in the store than before.*
 
 
 
• "**Much more**" is used when referring to uncountable or non-specific quantities, such as abstract concepts or substances that can't be easily counted.
 
 
• **For example-** *She needs much more patience to complete this project.*
 
 
 
• *​*The word "**thought**" is being quantified in the given sentence, and since "**thought**" refers to an abstract concept that cannot be counted, "**much more**" is the appropriate phrase to use.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

**The sentence should read:** *Before he could devote much more thought to the matter, Pranav had stepped up to him.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2**: The name "**Pranav**" is correctly placed in the sentence.
 
• **Option 3**: The verb "**had stepped up**" is also correctly used in the sentence.
